```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,fig.width = 7,fig.height = 5)
library(tidyverse)
```

### My Choice of Genes

* Genes: GNLY, LYN, IL26
* Continuous covariate: mat_vitD(vitamin D, ng/mL)
* Categorical covariate 1: bmi_group
* Cateforical covariate 2: preg_preeclampsia (Normal vs. Preeclampsia)

**Why these tow new genes?**  I screened the genes that are in the expression file 
for an association with vitamin D and with preeclampsia, and picked two that behave 
differently from GNLY.
* LYN goes up with vitamin D (GNLY goes down) and is expressed at a high level.
* IL26 is expressed at a very low level, so its y-axis is on a completely 
different scale.

### Step1. Load the raw data

```{r load}
#read.csv with row.names = 1 uses the first column (probe IDs) as row names
covar <- read.csv(file = 'GSE85307_covar-1.csv')
geneNames <- read.csv(file = 'GSE85307_geneNames.csv')
expr <- read.csv(file = 'GSE85307_geneExpression.csv', row.names = 1)

# The first column name of the covariate file can come in with a hidden extra
# character (BOM), so we rename it ourselves
colnames(covar)[1] <- 'subjectID'

# Look at the the structure
str(covar)
dim(expr)
head(geneNames)
```
### Step 2. Clean the covariates

Every covariate value is stored as text with a label, like "age_year: xxx". I
remove everything up to and including ":" and then fix the data types.

```{r clean}
# Loop through columns 3 to 10 (all covariates; columns 1-2 are the IDs)
# '.*: ' means "any characters followed by a colon and a space"
for(i in colnames(covar)[3:10]){
  covar[,i] <- sub(pattern = '.*: ',replacement = '', x = covar[,i])
}
head(covar)

# Numeric variables
covar$mat_age_yrs <- as.numeric(covar$mat_age_yrs)
covar$delivery_gestAge_wks <- as.numeric(covar$delivery_gestAge_wks)
covar$sampleCollection_gestAge_wks <- as.numeric(covar$sampleCollection_gestAge_wks)
covar$mat_BMI <- as.numeric(covar$mat_BMI)
covar$mat_vitD <- as.numeric(covar$mat_vitD)

# Categorical variables
covar$preg_preeclampsia <- factor(covar$preg_preeclampsia,
                                  levels = c('Normal','Preeclampsia'))
covar$mat_asthma <- factor(ifelse(covar$mat_asthma=='1','Asthma','Healthy'))

# Check that the types and values look right
str(covar)
summary(covar)
```
### Step 3. Derive a categorical variable from a continuous one

```{r derive}
# BMI groups: <25, 25-30, >=30
# Only 5 women have the BMI < 18.5, too few for their own group, so they are 
# combined with the "<25" group
covar$bmi_group <- cut(covar$mat_BMI,
                       breaks = c(0,25,30,Inf),
                       labels = c('<25','25-30','>=30'))

# Check the sample sizes
table(covar$bmi_group,covar$preg_preeclampsia)

```

### Step 4. Build one data frame with all three genes

```{r match}
genesOfInterest <- c('GNLY','LYN','IL26')

# Gene name <- probe ID
probeLookup <- geneNames[geneNames$GENE %in% genesOfInterest,]
probeLookup$PROBEID <- as.character(probeLookup$PROBEID)

# Make sure there is exactly one probe per gene and all are in the 
# expression data (all True). Only 500 of the 750 genes in geneNames are in expr.
nrow(probeLookup)
table(probeLookup$PROBEID %in% rownames(expr))

# Transpose so smaples are rows
exprT <- t(expr)

# Startt from the covariates and add one column per gene
plotData <- covar
for(i in genesOfInterest){
  # Find the probe ID for this gene
  probeID <- probeLookup[probeLookup$GENE==i,'PROBEID']
  # Pull out the gene's values, ordering the samples by the covariate geoIDs
  # so that each row of the covariates gets its own sample's expression
  plotData[,i] <- as.numeric(exprT[plotData$geoID,probeID])
}

# Check there are no missing values (all F)
table(is.na(plotData[,genesOfInterest]))

# Spot check one sample for each gene against the raw expression table(all T)
for(i in genesOfInterest){
  probeID <- probeLookup[probeLookup$GENE==i,'PROBEID']
  print(expr[probeID,plotData$geoID[1]]==plotData[1,i])
}

head(plotData[,c('geoID','mat_vitD','bmi_group','preg_preeclampsia',genesOfInterest)])
```

### Step 5. The function


```{r function}
plotGeneExpression <- function(data,geneList,contVar,catVars) {
  
  # Define color palette
  colorPalette <- c('grey50','darkgreen')
  
  # Define theme 
  myTheme <- theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = 'top',
          plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
          plot.title.position = 'plot')
  
  # Define somewhere to store the plots
  myPlots <- list()
  
  # Loop through all genes
  for (i in geneList) {
    
    # Plot 1: histogram of gene expression
    # (.data[[i]] turns the gene name, which is text, into the column of that name)
    p1 <- ggplot(data,aes(x = .data[[i]])) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 20,fill = 'darkgreen',color = 'white') +
      labs(title = paste('Distribution of',i,'Expression'),
           x = paste(i,'Expression'),y = 'Number of Samples') +
      myTheme
    
    # Plot 2: continuous covariate vs. gene expression
    p2 <- ggplot(data,aes(x = .data[[contVar]],y = .data[[i]])) +
      geom_point() +
      # Add linear fit with shaded error
      geom_smooth(method = lm,formula = y ~ x,color = 'darkgreen',fill = 'darkgreen') +
      # Leave empty space at the top of the plot for the correlation
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05,0.2))) +
      # Add the Pearson correlation
      ggpubr::stat_cor(method = 'pearson') +
      labs(title = paste(i,'Expression vs.',contVar),
           x = contVar,y = paste(i,'Expression')) +
      myTheme
    
    # Plot 3: boxplot by both categorical variables
    p3 <- ggplot(data,aes(x = .data[[catVars[1]]],y = .data[[i]],
                          fill = .data[[catVars[2]]])) +
      # outlier.shape = NA because every sample is drawn as a point below
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
      geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15)) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = colorPalette) +
      labs(title = str_wrap(paste(i,'Expression by',catVars[1],'and',catVars[2]),
                            width = 45),
           x = catVars[1],y = paste(i,'Expression'),fill = catVars[2]) +
      myTheme
    
    # Store the 3 plots for this gene
    myPlots[[i]] <- list('histogram' = p1,'scatter' = p2,'boxplot' = p3)
  }
  
  # Return the list of plots
  myPlots
}
```


### Step 6. Run the function

```{r run}
# One call makes all 9 plots (3 plots x 3 genes)
genePlots <- plotGeneExpression(data = plotData,
                                geneList = genesOfInterest,
                                contVar = 'mat_vitD',
                                catVars = c('bmi_group','preg_preeclampsia'))

# Look at the structure of what the function returned
names(genePlots)
names(genePlots$GNLY)

# Save every plot, e.g. submission2_GNLY_histogram.png
for (i in names(genePlots)) {
  for (j in names(genePlots[[i]])) {
    ggsave(filename = paste0('submission2_',i,'_',j,'.png'),
           plot = genePlots[[i]][[j]],width = 7,height = 5)
  }
}
```
